subsystems.name: Elevated mounting structure
subsystems.role: holds the array high enough for crops, people and farm machinery to pass underneath.

subsystems.name: PV array
subsystems.role: converts the light the crop does not need into electricity.

subsystems.name: Crop system
subsystems.role: the agricultural half of the dual yield.
parts: row layout matched to module rows

subsystems.name: Water and microclimate management
subsystems.role: turns the shading into an advantage instead of a problem.
parts: gutters and drip lines that redirect module runoff

subsystems.name: Electrical collection and grid connection
subsystems.role: delivers power from a field-scale array.

subsystems.name: Dual-yield monitoring
subsystems.role: proves both harvests are actually happening.

buildSteps.title: Model the light
buildSteps.detail: Engineers calculate how much photosynthetically active radiation reaches the canopy for a given module height, tilt, row gap and orientation, then match that to what the chosen crop can tolerate.

buildSteps.title: Design the agronomic layout
buildSteps.detail: Row spacing and orientation are set so tractors, sprayers and harvesters can work beneath the array without hitting posts or modules.

buildSteps.title: Build the foundations
buildSteps.detail: Posts are driven or ballasted into place, tall enough to leave roughly 3–4 m of clearance under the lowest module edge.

buildSteps.title: Install the modules
buildSteps.detail: Bifacial modules are mounted at a tilt that balances crop light against energy yield, wired in strings to inverters at the field edge.

buildSteps.title: Rework the water
buildSteps.detail: Gutters and drip lines collect the water that sheds off the modules and spread it evenly rather than concentrating it in drip lines that erode soil or starve the strip under each row.

buildSteps.title: Connect to the grid
buildSteps.detail: Transformers and metering are installed and the array is commissioned alongside the irrigation system.

buildSteps.title: Test the pairing
buildSteps.detail: The first seasons are used to measure crop yield, soil moisture and electricity output together, so the design can be adjusted.

buildSteps.title: Operate as one farm
buildSteps.detail: Mowing, spraying and harvest are scheduled around both outputs; panel cleaning and washing are timed to avoid the crop.

prerequisites.why: the economics only work if the modules are a small share of total cost, since output per hectare is deliberately reduced.
the steel to lift modules several metres is the main capital premium over a normal solar farm.

prerequisites.tech: Knowledge of crop response to partial shade
prerequisites.why: shade-tolerant crops are well understood, but the exact light level that maximises combined food-plus-energy yield is not.

prerequisites.tech: Farm machinery that fits under the array
prerequisites.why: standard tractors and harvesters need wide, straight corridors, which constrains array density and thus energy output.
many jurisdictions treat farmland solar and agriculture as mutually exclusive land uses.

pathway.milestone: commercial and research agrivoltaic plots for grapes, berries, vegetables and pasture, mostly in Europe and Asia
pathway.unlocks: real data on combined land productivity.

pathway.milestone: standardised, crop-specific array designs, including single-axis trackers that follow the sun while keeping light on the crop
pathway.unlocks: predictable yields for farmers and lenders.

pathway.milestone: rainwater harvesting and irrigation integrated into the mounting structure
pathway.unlocks: viable dual use in drier regions where water, not light, is the limit.

pathway.milestone: agrivoltaics treated as normal farm infrastructure
pathway.unlocks: farm income diversification and solar build-out without competing for land.
